claims.section: A sanitized first-party case on publishing a governed AI whitepaper without exposing the private blueprint

claims.claim_summary: This case study shows how a public research artifact can move from outcome definition through planning, assurance, publication, public readback, and closeout while preserving proprietary implementation boundaries.
This case covers the public release of BRAIZ Works Research WP-02, *The Enterprise Execution Gap*.

The intended outcome was not merely “write a whitepaper.” It was to create a public-safe research artifact that could serve community education and enterprise social proof while preserving first-party intellectual property boundaries.

The project separated planning, producer qualification, independent review, owner acceptance, freeze, publication authorization, deployment, public verification, social disposition, and final closeout.

The publication canary surfaced several practical failure modes before the broader portfolio was batched: hidden-file upload friction, accidental path duplication, platform-specific Pages enablement, release-asset assembly, and the need to preserve exact owner authority for consequential lifecycle transitions.
The published paper explains enterprise assurance principles—authority, evidence, lifecycle, recovery, change control, and independent review—without exposing the exact system that implements them.
Once the WP-02 canary proved the publication mechanics, running nine more papers through nine fully serial pipelines would duplicate shared work.
claims.section: Why the portfolio moved to batching

claims.claim_summary: A public case study should record: exact outcome, source boundary, lifecycle path, evidence classes, material failures and repairs, measured versus modeled quantities, privacy/IP constraints, limitations, and what was deliberately not disclosed.
This is a first-party case and therefore should not be treated as an independent market study.
